programme.title: Walking Britain's Roman Roads
programme.desc: When the Romans invaded Britain, they needed to march armies long distances to keep order. Dan Jones travels the length of their first project, Watling Street.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Roman Roads
programme.desc: Dan Jones follows the route of Ermine Street which ran from London to York, through Lincolnshire and Cambridgeshire and subsequently linked Castleford with Doncaster, Littleborough and Lincoln.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Roman Roads
programme.desc: Dan Jones explores Dere Street, which ran from York into Scotland. The Romans founded the city of York, primarily to house thousands of soldiers but more importantly as a base for invasion into the north.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Roman Roads
programme.desc: Dan Jones travels along Fosse Way, for 370 kms through the heart of England. The Latin word for ditch, "fossa", is likely to have inspired its name.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Roman Roads
programme.desc: Dan Jones travels the historic Roman road of Ermin Way, which links the two Roman towns of Calleva Atrebatum and Glevum, now known as Silchester and Gloucester.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Roman Roads
programme.desc: Dan Jones travels along Stane Street, which runs 107 kms from London to Chichester, and discovers what lead the Romans to abandon Britain in the Fifth Century AD.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Lost Railways
programme.desc: This episode takes Rob on a Scottish adventure along the old route from Elgin to Portsoy, a lost line which served the fishing and whisky industries so vital to the local communities.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Lost Railways
programme.desc: This week Rob starts his journey in the famous steel town of Sheffield where he'll be following the old Woodhead Line through the Pennines to the industrial powerhouse of Manchester.

programme.title: Walking Britain's Lost Railways
programme.desc: Rob's journey through Dartmoor from Plymouth to Exeter begins in unlikely surrounds: in the garage of model railway enthusiast Bruce Hunt.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo strikes out to explore the Britain of his youth. He's a 'boomer', born in the decade after the end of the Second World War, and he recalls the excitement of rebuilding the nation.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael's railway journey through northwest Britain from Preston to Hebden Bridge reaches Greater Manchester, where he celebrates new beginnings for the nation in the years after the Second World War.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Greater Manchester's Metrolink tram delivers Michael to the former cotton town of Oldham on the edge of the Peak District. He then takes the Hope Valley Line to Edale to enjoy the national park.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: In Wakefield, West Yorkshire, Michael visits the National Coal Mining Museum at Caphouse Colliery. His guide, an ex-miner, takes him 140 metres down into the mine to imagine the conditions men faced.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his post-war exploration of northwest England in Bradford, Shipley and Hebden Bridge. In Centenary Square in Bradford, Michael encounters literary giant, J.B. Priestley.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael travels through the Britain of his youth from London's Docklands and East End to the 'city within a city', the Barbican. At Tilbury, he traces the arrival in 1948 of the Empire Windrush.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his railway exploration of the post-war Britain of his youth on a journey from London to Cambridge.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo ventures deep underground onto London's newest railway: the Elizabeth Line. From the driver's cab he enjoys an impressively smooth ride from Paddington to Tottenham Court Road.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his rail exploration of the east of England from London's Tilbury docks to Cambridge.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael completes his railway journey through the east of England during the post-war period. At RAF Lakenheath, he discovers a slice of America dropped into the British countryside.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael begins in the city of Derby at its famous 19th century railway works, he hears how the Victorian sheds now house some of the latest assembly lines in Britain for building electric trains.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Beginning this time in Coventry, Michael recalls the destruction by the German Luftwaffe of the city's gothic cathedral. He hears how architect Basil Spence won a competition to build it anew.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael railway journey through the Midlands and West Country reaches the heart of the Warwickshire countryside, where the on-going construction of Britain's biggest railway project takes place.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael stops in Wolverhampton where the ever-increasing demand for workers during the post war boom years saw immigrants from the Caribbean and South Asia arrive in Britain.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo is on the last leg of his journey from the train-building in Derby to the aircraft manufacturing base of Filton. From Tewkesbury in Gloucestershire, he heads to Eastnor castle.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore the shortest branch line on the London Underground network. The disused stretch of the Picadilly line ran for just a third of a mile between Holborn and Aldwych.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway visit one of London Underground's most secret places: North End under Hampstead Heath. Abandoned before completion, the station became a Cold War bunker.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore the disused parts of Piccadilly Circus, the grandest station on the London Underground. And they also visit the long-abandoned Highgate surface station.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore the hidden parts of Euston, including unique features not found elsewhere and the bits set for demolition for HS2. Siddy also visits York Road station.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway have a night-time track walk exploring long forgotten stations on the District line in Whitechapel. And they discover how sprawling Oxford Circus was first built.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore Clapham South deep level shelter, where thousands of Londoners slept in the war. They also visit Moorgate, and the remains of a tunnelling machine there.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim and Siddy continue to uncover the mysteries of the London Underground by exploring the disused Jubilee line areas of Charing Cross station and its new claim to fame as a film location.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway continue their exploration of the London Underground by uncovering the hidden world of the Waterloo and City line, the only line that is entirely underground.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore King William Street, the original terminus of the first electric Tube in the world.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim and Siddy walk the Piccadilly line to explore hidden World War II remains of Brompton Road, a station that played a strategic role in the Capital's defences against the German Luftwaffe.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore the disused parts of London Bridge. Siddy visits Ongar in Essex and nearby Blake Hall.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore Kings Cross St Pancras, including a secret siding and the disused Thameslink station.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway explore the brand new Elizabeth Line and have access to two of its stations weeks before the line opens.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim and Siddy travel 50 miles from London to visit Quainton Road in Buckinghamshire, a railway station that was once part of the London underground.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.desc: Tim Dunn and Siddy Holloway visit the cathedral-like Greenwich Power Station, which stands ready to power the tube at short notice.

programme.title: Secrets of the London Underground
programme.sub-title: Baker Street And Edgware Road Signal Cabin
programme.desc: Railway historian Tim Dunn teams up with Siddy Holloway from the London Transport Museum to explore the disused parts of London's tube network.
